chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, who raised it, saying:

A woman asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said: “I used to remain seated during my nifās for twenty days, until they gave me a ruling of eighteen days.” So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Why did they give you a ruling of eighteen days?” She said: “Because of the hadith that was narrated from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, that he said to Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays when she gave birth to Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr.”

Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Asmāʾ asked the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم when eighteen days had already passed for her; had she asked him before that, he would have instructed her to perform ghusl and do as the mustahādah does.”

We have fully covered what relates to this chapter in our larger book; whoever wants it may find it there. As for what has been narrated regarding precautionary waiting for the woman in nifās by a day or two, its meaning is what we mentioned in the ruling of the mustahādah: that she takes it into consideration when her habit in menstruation is less than ten days, but when it reaches ten, then there is no precautionary waiting. And what has been narrated that she observes precautionary waiting by the like of two-thirds of her days is also of this kind, when her habit is five or six days; likewise what has been said that she observes precautionary waiting by the like of two-thirds of the days of her nifās. All of that we have cited in our larger book and clarified the correct aspect of it there.

key_terms.الِاسْتِظْهَارِ: precautionary waiting beyond the usual habit to determine the ruling
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, whose legal duties differ from nifās and hayd
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا: eighteen days, mentioned here as the time at which the question was asked
key_terms.عَادَتُهَا: her established habit or customary duration
key_terms.عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: ten days, the threshold referenced in the legal discussion
key_terms.نِفَاسِي: my postpartum bleeding state after childbirth

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the maximum duration of nifās in Shia hadith, and how is the report of Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays understood?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal ruling on the maximum days of nifās and clarifies that the report concerning eighteen days for Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays does not establish eighteen as a fixed limit. Rather, the Imam عليه السلام explains that had she asked earlier, she would have been instructed to perform ghusl and act as a mustahādah, and the later discussion addresses how precautionary waiting applies in relation to a woman's menstrual habit.
